Good morning, church. Would you turn with me in your Bibles to Isaiah chapter 40. We're going to read verse 31 together. But they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint.

Now I want you to notice something about that verse. It doesn't say they that hurry upon the Lord. It doesn't say they that worry upon the Lord. It says they that wait. And waiting is the one thing none of us wants to do. We live in a world of next-day delivery and instant answers, and then we come to God and we expect Him to work on our schedule.

But here's the truth I want you to take home this morning: waiting on God is not wasted time. Waiting on God is where the strength comes from. The eagle doesn't flap its way to the top of the sky. It waits for the wind, and then it rises.

Some of you are in a waiting room right now. You're waiting on a diagnosis. You're waiting on a prodigal to come home. You're waiting on a job, on a healing, on an answer to a prayer you've prayed a hundred times. And you're tired. Isaiah says the young men shall utterly fall, but they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength.

Psalm 27:14 says the same thing. Wait on the Lord: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart. God is never late, but He is rarely early. So this week, when you're tempted to run ahead of Him, stop and remember: the waiting is the work. Let's pray.
